title.narrative: CRECO - Citizen Resilience Against Manipulation in Kenya
CRECO - Citizen Resilience Against Manipulation in Kenya

description.narrative:
In Kenya, digital democracy is particularly important due to the country's growing internet penetration and the increasing use of mobile technology. With over 43 million internet users as of 2023, digital platforms present a significant opportunity to engage young people in governance and political processes (Communications Authority of Kenya, 2023). However, the rise of digital platforms has also brought challenges, particularly in the spread of misinformation and fake news. Studies have shown that false information spreads rapidly on social media, exacerbating political tensions and influencing public perception. The digital democracy landscape in Kenya is thus a complex interplay of opportunities and challenges. While technology has enabled greater citizen participation and streamlined governance, it has also introduced new risks that need to be managed to ensure a healthy and functional democratic process. Understanding and combating misinformation and disinformation are crucial for maintaining the integrity of democratic processes. This project explores the definitions, sources, and motivations for misinformation, and its impact on democracy. It provides strategies to identify and respond to false information, with real-world examples and interactive class activities.
Project Goal: To promote digital democracy and enhance young people’s media literacy skills to enable them understand, recognize, verify and debunk dis/misinformation through a coordinated CSOs, academia and media response in tracking, countering negative narratives and engaging government on proposed policy recommendations. The primary objective of the project is to support joint efforts of civil society organizations, media, government, colleges and universities to enhance youth’s capacity in countering dis/misinformation and developing digital literacy skills
Specific objectives: a) To equip the public with skills to critically evaluate information and recognize misinformation and stop the spread of fake news b) To strengthen fact-checking mechanisms among CSOs, colleges/universities and media c) To advocate for policies that promote transparency and accountability in information dissemination
